learning_outcomes.text: Apply notions from basic knowledge of physics, thermodynamics and heat transfer, placing them in innovative contexts close to research areas.

Evaluate the best system solution in accordance with the needs of the users in terms of energy saving and optimisation of the economic return on investment, both in areas already known and in other broader and interdisciplinary aspects.
Integrate the knowledge acquired from other courses to appropriately formulate engineering solutions to problems in the field of energy.
Critically analyse projects of existing cogeneration units, evaluating their strengths and weaknesses, effectiveness and efficiency, environmental impact and economic sustainability.
Compare different plant solutions aimed at energy recovery, evaluating their effectiveness and efficiency in terms of energy savings, emission reductions and investment costs.
Research and analyse data on national and international energy policies, evaluating their objectives, the instruments used and the results obtained.

Communicate one's own ideas and engineering solutions to expert interlocutors, as well as transfer the same information to users who are not experts in the field of energy but who nevertheless have to interface with problems of this nature.
Develop the ability to collaborate, communicate and solve problems effectively within a team.
Communicate effectively with customers, understand their needs and provide them with clear and concise information.
Solve problems in the field of energy using the tools learnt in the course, as well as show the ability to apply the broader notions learnt in their course of study to solve innovative case studies.
Tackle problems in designing and operating cogeneration units independently, developing strategies for analysis, evaluation and choice of the most suitable solutions.
Apply theoretical knowledge to concrete cases, developing practical skills and problem-solving abilities through laboratory activities and simulations.
Integrate knowledge from different disciplines (engineering, economics, environment) to address the complexity of cogeneration unit projects, developing a holistic view of the energy sector.
Research and critically evaluate information on different plant solutions, developing analysis and discernment skills.
Compare different plant solutions regarding performance, cost and environmental impact, developing critical evaluation skills and conscious choice.
Keep abreast of the latest technologies and plant solutions in the energy recovery sector, developing a capacity for continuous learning.
Analyse data and statistics related to energy policies, developing skills of interpretation and critical evaluation of data.
Discuss and debate on topical energy issues, developing argumentation, communication, and critical thinking skills.
Develop proposals and solutions to improve existing energy policies, developing problem-solving skills and creative thinking.

syllabus_topics: Energy economics, energy supply and fossil fuels
Evaluation methods for energy optimisation of plants
Economic feasibility studies of energy saving measures
Solar thermal systems: plant solutions and design methods
Cogeneration and trigeneration: operating characteristics and management of a cogeneration system
assessment_rules: For mechanical students, the written test lasts two hours and consists of two exercises, each worth 15 points. The written test is passed if a minimum threshold of 18 points is reached. The oral test consists of three questions and requires a minimum of 18 points, assessing correctness of answer (1-9 points) and method/language (0-3 points). For the final mark, the written test is weighted 50% and the oral test 50%. For management students, the assessment is an oral test consisting of three questions, with a minimum threshold of 18 points, and a project test, each weighted 50% for the final grade.
